searchEngine.finding: Existing job store, runner, ownership audit, pause/cancel/resume, results, promotion, research loop, and evaluation policies remain the authoritative engine state machine.

browserHarnesses.finding: Existing V2 final harness reuses one stateful production server and fixed ports across viewports. Its browser records do not implement the required isolated runtime lifecycle or complete machine-verifiable field set.

persistedReports.finding: Historical reports conflict. The newest dedicated final V2 report says NOT VERIFIED and skipped quality gates; older reports claim narrower success. No previous completion claim is accepted as current evidence.

plannerV2.finding: Required directory and versioned PlanV2 authority do not exist. Some draft/hash/diff helpers exist inside reasoning and V1 modules only.

tasksApprovalOrchestration.finding: Required task authority, approval invalidation, dependency ordering, restart reconciliation, and multi-tab conflict model do not yet exist as focused modules.

eventLifecycle.finding: Tool events are in-memory; the required persisted, replayable cross-engine event layer and autonomous reconciliation are absent.

memoryReflection.finding: No server-authoritative bounded long-term decision/outcome memory or post-outcome reflection subsystem exists.

deadModules.finding: No module was proven dead strongly enough to remove during this audit; preservation rules forbid speculative cleanup.

04_everyRootCauseFound: V1 and V2 shared a large control-plane route, so stale page/chat authority could override server execution state.
Historical browser harnesses reused runtime/server state across viewports, polluting active-job selection and approval evidence.
Client hydration and delayed React refs could resurrect stale proposals or send stale/null entity context on fast follow-up turns.
There was no persisted PlanV2/task authority, no one-active-write-task invariant, and no restart reconciliation layer.
Tool lifecycle events were process-memory only, preventing replayable monitoring and refresh recovery.
There was no bounded evidence-linked long-term memory or terminal-outcome reflection authority.
Paper lifecycle and strategy library controls were missing from the safe tool surface.
Provider response-body aborts could escape the request catch after headers arrived, producing a 500 instead of fallback.
Approved execution context could be overwritten by stale route context, and approval could trigger unnecessary provider work.
Result promotion existed as a handler but had no conversational intent/plan, and its jobId was misread as a newly started search in completion prose.
Acceptance instrumentation reused a post-execution hasApproval field and retained an obsolete two-provider-attempt expectation after search status became deterministic.
